vocab:
Format: VOCABULARY UPGRADE ('Say THIS, Not THAT' / Psychological Curiosity Hook).
CRITICAL RULE: DO NOT mention any explicit level codes or labels (such as 'C1', 'C2', 'B1', 'B2', 'Advanced Level', 'Beginner Level') in the title, subtitle, badge, scripts, narration, examples, or captions. Create high intrigue purely through psychological curiosity gaps and practical value.
Difficulty: MODERATE & RELATABLE (Practical everyday vocabulary for work and life).
Pick ONE overused English word or phrase. ROTATE ACROSS THESE CATEGORIES - do not default to 'Very ___', which this account has already used many times:
  a) Intensifier pairs: 'really tired', 'so boring', 'super important'
  b) Weak verbs: 'get', 'do', 'make', 'say', 'go' used where a precise verb exists
  c) Filler openers: 'I think', 'kind of', 'a lot of', 'basically'
  d) Flat adjectives: 'nice', 'good', 'bad', 'interesting', 'fine'
  e) Workplace filler: 'ASAP', 'touch base', 'just checking in'
  f) Overused connectors: 'and then', 'but', 'also' where a stronger link exists
Only use a 'Very ___' phrase if the hook-variety rules below do not ban it.
Provide 3 natural, practical alternatives that native speakers use every day.
Intro Hook Styles to use:
- 'Stop saying [Basic Phrase] if you want to sound fluent.'
- 'POV: You want to sound like a native English speaker.'
- 'Say THIS, not THAT in everyday English!'
- '3 natural phrases that make you sound instantly more confident.'

Fields required in JSON:
- 'badge': 'VOCABULARY BOOST'
- 'title': 'Stop Saying "[Overused Phrase]"'
- 'subtitle': 'Say THIS, Not THAT 🗣️'
- 'intro_script': 'Stop saying [Overused Phrase]! Here are three natural phrases to sound instantly more fluent.'
- 'items': List of 3 objects, each with:
    * 'basic': str (the overused basic phrase)
    * 'advanced': str (single punchy, natural alternative word/phrase)
    * 'nuance': str (simple 3-5 word practical feeling/meaning)
    * 'example': str (clear, natural everyday sentence)
    * 'narration': str (spoken script for this specific word, e.g. 'Number one: Swamped. Use this when you have too much work piling up. For example: I am totally swamped with emails today.')
- 'outro_script': 'Which phrase was your favorite? Save this reel for practice and comment your sentence below!'
- 'instagram_caption': High-converting caption with psychological hook ('❌ Stop saying this...'), bullet breakdown, '💾 Save for later', and 15+ hashtags.

quiz:
Format: HIGH-CHALLENGE 3-SECOND ENGLISH QUIZ (Extreme Curiosity Gap & Ego Hook).
CRITICAL RULE: DO NOT mention any explicit level codes or labels (such as 'C1', 'C2', 'B1', 'B2', 'Advanced Level', 'Beginner Level') in the title, subtitle, badge, scripts, narration, examples, or captions. Create high intrigue purely through psychological curiosity gaps and practical value.
Difficulty: HIGH CHALLENGE & TRICKY (Test subtle grammar traps, tricky dependent prepositions, subtle collocations, subjunctive, inversions, or confusing homophones that trip up 95% of English speakers).
Examples of High-Challenge Quiz Topics:
- Tricky dependent prepositions: 'conducive _', 'compliant _', 'accustomed _', 'deprived _', 'prone _'
- Inversions & Correlatives: 'Hardly had we arrived _ it started raining' (when vs than vs that), 'No sooner had I left _'
- Subjunctive & Modals: 'It is vital that she _ informed immediately' (be vs is vs was)
- Confusing verbs: 'lay vs lie', 'rise vs raise', 'affect vs effect in context'

CRITICAL FORMATTING RULE FOR QUIZ:
Use STRICTLY a single underscore '_' for the blank in the question sentence (e.g. 'This environment is not conducive _ productivity.'). DO NOT use multiple underscores.

Psychological Curiosity Hook Styles for Quiz (Pick one punchy ego hook):
- '95% of English speakers fail this quiz!'
- 'Think you're fluent? Only 5% get this right on the first try.'
- 'The #1 grammar trap that fools even smart speakers.'
- 'Can you solve this tricky English puzzle in 3 seconds?'
- '99% of people choose the wrong answer here. What's yours?'

Fields required in JSON:
- 'badge': '3-SEC TRICKY QUIZ'
- 'title': '95% of People Fail This Quiz!' (or similar high-intrigue curiosity title)
- 'question': Tricky question sentence using STRICTLY a single '_' for the blank
- 'options': Array of 4 tempting options with plausible distractors ['A) to', 'B) for', 'C) with', 'D) in']
- 'correct_option': 'A'
- 'correct_text': 'A) to'
- 'explanation': Short, brilliant explanation of the underlying grammar rule or collocation.
- 'intro_script': '95% of English speakers fail this challenge! Fill in the blank: [read sentence using the word "blank" for "_"]. Can you solve this before the timer runs out?'
- 'countdown_script': 'Three, two, one...'
- 'reveal_script': 'The correct answer is [correct text]! [clear punchy explanation]. Did you beat the timer? Drop your answer in the comments and save this reel!'
- 'instagram_caption': High-converting caption with ego curiosity hook ('95% get this wrong...'), the question, countdown teaser, correct answer breakdown, 'Save for later', and 15+ hashtags.

corporate:
Format: CORPORATE & WORKPLACE ENGLISH (High Content Density - 4 Executive Phrase Swaps).
CRITICAL RULE: DO NOT mention any explicit level codes or labels (such as 'C1', 'C2', 'B1', 'B2', 'Advanced Level', 'Beginner Level') in the title, subtitle, badge, scripts, narration, examples, or captions. Create high intrigue purely through psychological curiosity gaps and practical value.

Pick a high-performing corporate theme, such as:
- 'How to Sound Professional in Emails'
- 'How to Politely Say NO at Work'
- 'How to Disagree Politely in Meetings'
- 'Phrases to Sound Like a Leader at Work'
- 'Corporate Buzzwords Translated into Plain English'

Provide exactly 4 punchy, high-value phrase upgrades (Casual/Blunt ➔ Executive Professional).
Examples:

Intro Hook Styles to use:
- 'POV: You want to sound professional in meetings & emails.'
- '4 Corporate English phrases that make you sound like an executive.'
- 'How to sound 10x more professional in workplace emails.'

- 'items': List of 4 objects, each with:

card:
Format: SINGLE PREMIUM CARD POST (Clean cheat-sheet card + trending music, NO voiceover).
CRITICAL RULE: DO NOT mention any explicit level codes or labels (such as 'C1', 'C2', 'B1', 'B2', 'Advanced Level', 'Beginner Level') in the title, subtitle, badge, scripts, narration, examples, or captions. Create high intrigue purely through psychological curiosity gaps and practical value.
This is a VISUAL-ONLY card (no narration). The content must be super concise & scannable.
Pick ONE common overused English phrase and provide exactly 5 punchy, natural alternatives.
Examples of card topics:
- 'Stop Saying Very Good' (Excellent, Outstanding, Superb, Remarkable, Exceptional)
- 'Stop Saying Very Tired' (Exhausted, Drained, Wiped out, Beat, Burnt out)
- 'Stop Saying Very Angry' (Furious, Livid, Fuming, Outraged, Seething)
- 'Stop Saying I Think' (I believe, I reckon, In my view, I'd say, It seems to me)

Fields required in JSON:
- 'badge': 'ENGLISH TIP'
- 'title': 'Stop Saying [Overused Phrase]' (short, punchy)
- 'items': List of exactly 5 objects, each with:
    * 'wrong': str (the overused phrase, e.g. 'Very Good')
    * 'right': str (the single-word or short natural alternative)
    * 'emoji': str (one relevant emoji for visual flair)
    * 'example': str (ONE short, natural sentence using the alternative, MAX 8 words.
      The card image has no room for these - they go in the caption, and they are
      what makes the post worth saving. Make each one concrete and everyday.)
- 'footer_cta': '💾 Save & Share with a friend!'
- 'instagram_caption': A SHORT hook and why the swap matters - 2 to 3 sentences.
  Do NOT list the five alternatives and do NOT write example sentences in the caption:
  the alternatives and their examples are appended automatically from 'items'.
